conflicts.description: Where the bulbs of solenoid 14, Insert Flash-Lamps, are mounted. The solenoid table routes BRN-BLU SOL. 14 (Q59, CPU 1P12-7) through the playfield plug 8P3-14, in the same column that sends 11 to the power supply (3P7-1) and 15 and 16 to the cabinet (7P1), which puts its load on or under the playfield; the known-working script lights only a backglass rocket-plume flasher from it (SolCallback(14) = "SetLamp 103," with Lampz 103 = BGFL40a) and nothing on the playfield, and the manual itself calls the backbox lamps 39 and 40 'Insert Panel'. The solenoid location drawing gives 14 no balloon, and the playfield wiring diagram's 8L14 designator does not settle it because the same sheet gives the backbox GI relay and the cabinet bell 8L designators too. Runtime binding is not in doubt; the physical location and therefore the placement are. Resolution path: a photograph or wiring trace of a real Space Shuttle showing where the BRN-BLU SOL. 14 wire ends, at the backbox insert board or at playfield flash-lamp sockets (and how many bulbs), which an owner or restorer could supply; no source this project holds shows it.

mechanisms.behavior: Three balls. A drained ball falls into the outhole (9); the outhole kicker (1) lifts it onto the ball ramp (trough) under the apron, where balls rest on the lower (12), middle (11) and top (10) positions. Initialize 10, 11 and 12 closed and 9 open with all three balls home. The ball-ramp release (2) kicks the ball on 12 into the shooter lane, where it rests on 36 until the manual plunger launches it; the next ball rolls down onto 12. The ROM serves at game start (with the "T" reset 5, the 3-bank reset 6, the post down 8 and the game-on enable 23), after a ball is locked in an eject hole, and after the last ball in play drains.
mechanisms.label: Outhole, three-ball ramp and shooter lane

mechanisms.behavior: Two kick-out holes, left (16) and right (24), are locks. A ball resting in either one is held; the ROM flashes the space (9), shuttle (10) and insert (14) flash lamps and serves another ball from the ball ramp (2). With balls in both holes, the long-ramp shot (32) starts multi-ball: the ROM raises the post (7), fires the left eject (3) at once and the right eject (4) about 3 s later (gameplay run). IPDB lists 2-ball and 3-ball multiball. The ROM fires an eject only on its own schedule, so model each hole as a saucer that holds a ball until its coil fires, and release the hole's switch as the ball leaves.
mechanisms.label: Left and right eject-hole locks and multi-ball

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets along the long ramp's left side (33 lowest to 35 highest), each latching its normally open switch closed while down. One reset coil (6) raises the bank. The ROM resets it at game start and when all three are down; a host holds the targets down until the reset and then releases them. Completion increases the spinner value (manual game play) and, at factory settings, released the outlane gate (13) in the gameplay run.
mechanisms.label: 3-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: A single drop target in the centre of the S-H-U-T-T-L-E row, latching switch 20 closed while down, with its own reset coil (5). The ROM resets it at game start and, in the gameplay run, after the ramp bull's-eye (38). Hitting it last awards 100,000 bonus (manual); IPDB calls it a timed drop target.
mechanisms.label: "T" drop target

mechanisms.behavior: One post between the flippers, driven up by the up-post coil (7) and down by the down-post coil (8): a two-coil latching post with no position switch, so its state is the last coil fired. Default: down. The manual: a centre-ramp shot raises the heat shield. In the gameplay run the long-ramp shot (32) raised it at multi-ball, and game start and the left return lane (14) lowered it. Lamp 7 (two bulbs) lights the post.
mechanisms.label: Up post between the flippers (heat shield)

mechanisms.behavior: A holding coil (13) on the right outlane gate. Game-Adjustment #7 selects the old gate, which energizes to let the ball drain, or the new gate, which energizes to return the ball to the flipper; #4 sets whether it starts each turn or game open or closed. At factory settings the right outlane rollover (13) made the ROM energize the gate, which stayed held until the 3-bank was completed (gameplay run). Lamp 28 (Gate Open) shows its state.
mechanisms.label: Right outlane gate

The solenoid test does not step it. Strength and recovery are table-owned.
